results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the undeclared var.env reference in main.tf locals (only var.environment is declared) and proposes reverting line 12 to var.environment, matching the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit b756522 changed the local `app_name` to reference `var.env`, but the only declared input variable is `environment`, so `terraform validate` fails with 'Reference to undeclared input variable'.
key_evidence: [10:53:24] Error: Reference to undeclared input variable
[10:53:24] An input variable with the name "env" has not been declared.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/infra/main.tf line 12, restore the previous working reference: `app_name = "calculator-${var.environment}"`.
assumptions: Nothing outside sample-app (for example Jenkins job config or external tfvars) expects a variable named `env`; a grep of sample-app on the branch found no other references.
next_checks: Run `terraform fmt -check && terraform validate` in sample-app/infra after the fix
Confirm `terraform plan` outputs app_name = "calculator-dev" as on main
If renaming to `env` was the goal, rename the variable declaration as well, and update any -var/tfvars callers

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies that subtract() was changed to return a + b, causing test_subtract to fail with 14 != 6, and suggests reverting it to a - b while leaving the test unchanged, matching the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 4446cb4 ('Refactor calculator arithmetic helpers') changed subtract() in sample-app/app/calculator.py from 'return a - b' to 'return a + b', so subtract now adds and test_subtract fails.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/app/calculator.py, change subtract() back to 'return a - b' (revert the one-line change from commit 4446cb4). Leave the test unchanged.
next_checks: Re-run pytest locally on the fixed code and confirm all 5 tests pass
Confirm with the commit author that changing subtract's behaviour was not intended as part of the refactor
After the Test stage passes, confirm that the later stages (Terraform Plan, Smoke Test, Deploy), which were skipped, also pass

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the typo'd credentialsId 'deploy-tokn' in the Deploy stage and proposes changing it back to 'deploy-token' in sample-app/Jenkinsfile, matching the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 4a1b8a2 changed the Deploy stage's credential binding ID from 'deploy-token' to 'deploy-tokn', and no Jenkins credential has that ID. withCredentials failed before the deploy step could run.
key_evidence: ERROR: Could not find credentials entry with ID 'deploy-tokn'
Commit message: "Update deploy stage credential binding"
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/Jenkinsfile, Deploy stage, change credentialsId: 'deploy-tokn' back to credentialsId: 'deploy-token'.
assumptions: A credential with ID 'deploy-token' exists in Jenkins. This is inferred from main building green, not checked in Jenkins.
next_checks: Check in Jenkins > Manage Credentials that 'deploy-token' exists as a Secret text credential the calculator job can use.
After the fix, check that the Deploy stage prints 'Deploying calculator (token length: N)' with N > 0.

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the default SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS change from 3 to 90 exceeding the 1-minute stage timeout, and its first-recommended fix restores the default to 3, matching the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 220b4ad changed the default SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS in sample-app/scripts/smoke_test.py from 3 to 90, but the Smoke Test stage has a 1-minute timeout, so the script is always killed at about 60s and the build is aborted.
key_evidence: [10:54:12] Timeout set to expire in 1 min 0 sec
[10:54:13] Waiting 90s for the service to become healthy...
[10:55:12] Cancelling nested steps due to timeout
Jenkinsfile, stage('Smoke Test'): options { timeout(time: 1, unit: 'MINUTES') }
smoke_test.py: for second in range(1, WAIT_SECONDS + 1): time.sleep(1)
diagnosis.suggested_fix: Revert the default in sample-app/scripts/smoke_test.py to WAIT_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS", "3")). That brings the stage back well under its 1-minute timeout. If a slower environment really needs a longer wait, set SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS there instead of raising the default.
assumptions: There is no real service whose startup needs more than about 3s. The script only sleeps and never checks health, so a longer wait doesn't make it more accurate.
The 90s pytest collection in the Test stage ('5 passed in 90.55s') is slowness in the environment or the Jenkins agent, not this commit, which only changes smoke_test.py.
next_checks: Confirm with the commit author whether some environment actually needs a longer smoke wait. If it does, set SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS for that environment and keep the wait under the stage timeout.
Compare the Test stage duration with a recent main build to see whether the 90s pytest collection is normal or a separate performance problem.
After the revert, check that the Smoke Test stage finishes in a few seconds and that Deploy runs.
